To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GRAPES-1 and GRAPES-2 experiments have demonstrated the feasibility of the technique of using the Earth’s magnetic field to detect and measure air showers.

the GRAPES-2 experiment is the world’s largest and highest resolution air shower array, and has been used to detect the first evidence of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin (GZK) cut-off in the cosmic-ray spectrum.

GRAPES- 3 is a high-density air shower detector array with a total area of 0.1 km 2, designed to study the structure in the energy spectra of cosmic rays in the energy range 10 15 –10 17 eV with a statistical accuracy of ± 1.5% and a systematic uncertainty of 1.5%.
